qualitativeClaims.claim: Relative velocity of police car with respect to speeding car is v_rel = u_p - v_c + a_p*t = -20 + 2t; it is zero at t=10 s, when the gap is maximum.
The gap between cars is the integral of relative velocity: g(t) = 20t - t^2, a downward parabola with maximum at t=10 s.
Police car catches the speeding car when positions are equal: 20t = t^2, giving t=20 s (excluding t=0).
At catch-up, police car speed is twice the constant speed of the speeding car.

givens.sourceText: boat moves at 4 m/s relative to the water

qualitativeClaims.claim: Take north as +y and east as +x; the boat's heading has a westward component that cancels the eastward current.
qualitativeClaims.expected: v_b sin θ = v_r, so θ = arcsin(v_r/v_b) = arcsin(2/4) = 30° west of north

qualitativeClaims.claim: The northward component of the boat's ground velocity determines the crossing time.
qualitativeClaims.expected: v_n = v_b cos θ = sqrt(v_b² − v_r²) = sqrt(12) ≈ 3.464 m/s; t = w / v_n = 240/3.464 ≈ 69.3 s

qualitativeClaims.claim: The eastward drift over the crossing is zero, so the boat lands directly opposite the start point.
qualitativeClaims.expected: net eastward velocity = v_r − v_b sin θ = 2 − 4·sin 30° = 0

Banks are straight and parallel, so directly opposite means 240 m due north of the start.
